newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: THREDBO RESCUERS MAKE PROGRESS AS WET WEATHER ARRIVES
The coordinators of the Thredbo rescue effort believe they have located further bodies in the landslide debris and are digging towards them as wet weather sets in.
Rain and light sleet started falling at Thredbo this morning, much earlier than was initially forecast.
A landslide caused the collapse of two lodges at the New South Wales ski resort last week.
Another body, that of a woman, was removed from the debris a short time ago, bringing the confirmed death toll to 13.
Two bodies were taken from the rubble early this morning and police said further victims were located in what was a bedroom in the shattered Bimbadeen Lodge.
Five people remain missing.
Site controller, Police Superintendent Paul Chaplin, said rescue workers expected to remove further bodies over the next few hours.
"We know the general location of those bodies," he said.
"We have had engineers studying the layouts and the floor plans of the two lodges and we're fairly confident that we know the general location of those particular bodies."
VANSTONE SAYS PEOPLE CAN SURVIVE WORKING 15 HOURS A WEEK
Federal Education Minister Amanda Vanstone says she is confident people will be able to survive on what they earn from working 15 hours a week.
The Government has defined 15 hours as its minimum working time for what it calls a "real job".
Senator Vanstone said the idea was to make people independent of the welfare system.
"The international recognition, international standard that's been used for a very long time in Australia, is that if you work for just one hour a week you are not unemployed," she said.
"And we calculate that at about 15 hours a week that's when they will be virtually independent."
COURT CALLS FOR REFERENDUM ON STATE TAXES
Western Australian Premier Richard Court has called for a referendum to amend the constitution to restore certainty and balance in financing arrangements between the states and the Commonwealth.
Mr Court said yesterday's High Court decision that state franchise fees were unconstitutional had created immense uncertainty.
He said the states and territories have asked the Commonwealth to trigger safety net arrangements as a temporary measure.
But he said in the long run, a referendum should be called to amend the constitution.

"The time has come for the Federal Government to be pro-active in relation to these taxation matters, now putting a safety net in place to protect our current revenues is a stop-gap measure," he said.
"And the constitution must be amended so that we set in concrete the states' ability to raise the revenues that it needs to deliver the services for which it has responsibility."
FEDERAL GOVT TO SAFEGUARD NURSING HOME FEES
The Federal Government has announced details of the prudential scheme set up to safeguard up-front nursing home entry fees.
Family Services Minister Judi Moylan said the arrangments delivered on the commitment to ensure the strongest possible protection for residents' funds.
She said the accommodation bonds would be paid into a national, independent trustee-regulated fund.
The Minister said the fund would be professionally managed under a board made up of members from banking, legal and provider backgrounds.
She said nursing homes would receive the income earned by the entry fees.
Ms Moylan expected annual income generated by the bonds to reach about $130 million in the third or fourth year, rising to at least $1.5 billion within ten years.
She said the income would significantly increase the capacity of nursing homes and hostels to invest in maintaining and upgrading facilities.
COLLINS TO QUIT SHADOW CABINET TO REPRESENT THE TERRITORY
Northern Territory Senator Bob Collins is quitting Shadow Cabinet to move to the backbench.
Senator Collins is the only Territory Labor politician in Federal parliament.
He said it was too difficult to continue to represent the Territory's interests in parliament at the same time as meeting the busy schedule of a Shadow Minister.
"I want to place my responsibilities of representing the Territory first and it was obvious that either one of those jobs was suffering," he said.
He said that when the Territory was also represented by Labor's Warren Snowdon, the two of them divided the workload effectively.
But Senator Collins said he now lacked the resources to do both jobs well.
A spokesman for Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley said Senator Collins discussed his plans with Mr Beazley about a month ago.
"Late last year, it was becoming obvious that it couldn't go on," Senator Collins said.
"I spoke to Kim earlier this year, he asked me to stay on for a little longer - which I did - but it got to the point where it just couldn't go on."
Mr Beazley's office said there was no suggestion Senator Collins would quit Parliament and his experience would be useful in Senate Committee hearings.

The spokeman said a frontbench reshuffle would have to wait until Caucus met when Parliament returned, although the Shadow Ministry was likely to discuss the issue at a meeting on Friday. The Caucus has to vote on new appointments to the frontbench.
The reshuffle will also need to deal with Peter Baldwin's decision to return to the backbench, ahead of leaving Parliament at the next election.
BASE JUMPERS TO FACE COURT AFTER ACCIDENT
Three men will face court later this month after the death of a man in a base jumping accident on Monday at Bungonia Gorge near Goulburn, in northern New South Wales.
The man's parachute failed to open when he leapt off the 300 metre cliff.
He was the second BASE jumper to die at the site in four years.
It's believed he died instantly but it took rescue personnel more than 20 hours to retrieve his body.
Three other men successfully made the jump, but have now been charged with engaging in an unsafe act, in contravention of National Parks and Wildlife Service regulations.
The men, a 30-year-old from Cooma and two Victorians, aged 24 and 29, will appear in Goulburn Court on August 20.
